hook.line: So you finally moved over to Claude from ChatGPT.
hook.visual: Woman with a handheld mic in her kitchen; ChatGPT and Claude logos above a black box reading 'Claude vs ChatGPT simplified'; an arrow from ChatGPT to Claude slides in at about 1.9 s.

beats.what: Callout to people who just switched from ChatGPT to Claude, with both logos and a title box on screen.
A white arrow appears between the logos, pointing from ChatGPT to Claude.
Logos replaced by two orange column headers, 'Claude' and 'ChatGPT', that build up the comparison.
'Analytical' and 'Thoughtful' added under Claude as she says them.
'Conversational' added under ChatGPT; 'Challenge your thinking' under Claude.
The lists reset to a second pair: 'Deep analysis' vs 'Conversational'.
Second table complete: 'Human sounding' vs 'AI sounding'.
Orange 'Claude Cowork' logo card pops in as she mentions the coworker features.
Retro 'Claude Code' terminal card added below, teasing another video.
Cut to the payoff: 'Screenshot this' with both apps' privacy settings screenshots and the menu path to turn off training.

why_it_works: The opening line names one exact audience (people who just switched to Claude), so they feel the video is for them.
The comparison is built word by word in two columns at the top while she speaks (text in the top band 0.64 of the time), so the takeaway can be read with the sound off.
It ends on a practical, saveable screenshot (privacy settings path) with 'Screenshot this', which drives saves and shares (12.6k shares).
The Claude Code card at 32.7 s promises another video, a reason to follow.
weaknesses: Only 1 cut in 38.7 s (longest shot 34.93 s); the static medium shot relies entirely on the text builds for movement.
Word-by-word captions are tiny (caption height median 0.035) and sit on her chest, competing with the top-of-frame tables.
Quiet mix (-22.0 LUFS) for a talking piece.
for_robert: Copy the build-up comparison table: two column headers at the top that fill in word by word as he says each trait, and let Fred hold up the final 'screenshot this' card as the payoff.
